title: A co-tenant workload steals host CPU while the application looks almost healthy

problem.summary: An unrelated workload sharing the host consumes CPU. Application services are never themselves saturated, yet they are intermittently delayed because they wait their turn on a runqueue. User-facing latency moves only slightly, so dashboards look nearly normal and the cause is invisible above the kernel.
symptoms: mild, intermittent latency jitter across several unrelated services at once
no service is itself busy: per-container CPU is flat or falling
no new error signatures; requests still succeed
host CPU busy rises but is not exhausted, and host load rises moderately

discriminators.signal: where the CPU went (container CPU vs call-path role)
discriminators.this_problem: a container consumes steady CPU during the incident that it did not consume in the baseline, and it has NO caller/callee edges in the call graph
discriminators.not_this_problem: the extra CPU is consumed by a service that appears in the call graph
discriminators.evidence: MEASURED on noisy_neighbor_aggressive_steady_r1: the co-tenant consumed 2.00 cores (baseline 0.00) with no call-path edges. See evidence/measured_verdict_noisy_neighbor_r1.json

discriminators.this_problem: host busy cores rise but the host is NOT exhausted
discriminators.not_this_problem: host CPU is exhausted and many services degrade sharply together
discriminators.evidence: MEASURED on the same run: host busy cores 5.31 -> 7.96 (x1.5), i.e. headroom remained. See evidence/measured_verdict_noisy_neighbor_r1.json

unverified_do_not_claim.claim: the delayed services show a raised runnable_wait share (ready to run, waiting for a CPU)
unverified_do_not_claim.measurement: runnable_wait of the labelled culprit never exceeds 4% in ANY fault family (max 4.0% svc_mem_cap, 2.6% svc_cpu_cap); on the co-tenant run the highest runnable_wait across services was 1.6%. See evidence/wait_signature_all_families.json
unverified_do_not_claim.consequence: removed from the discriminators. Do not reinstate without new evidence.
unverified_do_not_claim.agent_note: A raised runnable-wait share on the delayed services. Measured across every labelled fault we have: this share never exceeds 4% for any fault type, and was 1.6% on the co-tenant case itself. It cannot separate anything - do not reason from it.

unverified_do_not_claim.claim: the wait decomposition of the culprit distinguishes this fault
unverified_do_not_claim.status: CANNOT BE MEASURED for this family
unverified_do_not_claim.measurement: this fault is labelled against the host, and L2 produces no record for 'host'. Across 93 runs there is no culprit-side L2 record for anomaly_cpu, anomaly_disk, anomaly_mem, anomaly_net or noisy_neighbor.
unverified_do_not_claim.consequence: either derive a host-level L2 record, or accept that this family is diagnosed from metrics + topology only.
unverified_do_not_claim.agent_note: The wait decomposition of the culprit. For host-attributed faults no culprit-side wait record exists at all, so its absence is meaningless here.

reproduction.system: Sock Shop or Train Ticket on Ubuntu 24.04, LTTng 2.15, Docker 27+, single GCP n2 VM

traces: server span duration per service, only to confirm the impact is mild
collection_order.why_these: MEASURED BASIS: the verified discriminators for this problem come from container CPU and the call graph, not from wait shares - runnable_wait was 1.6% on the co-tenant run and never exceeds 4% in any family (evidence/wait_signature_all_families.json). The scheduler events are still collected because they are what a host-level wait record WOULD be derived from, which is the open gap for this family.

processing.step: Stage the kernel trace so babeltrace2 can read it, because channels are stored gzipped
processing.expect: a CTF directory containing a metadata file and channel0_* streams

processing.step: Decode only the scheduler events inside the incident window
processing.expect: non-empty output; zero lines means the window is misaligned, because the trace is stamped in the host timezone while ground truth is UTC, so TZ=UTC is required

processing.step: Attribute per-service wall time to on-CPU, runnable-wait and blocked, using the container-to-PID map
processing.expect: one record per service, with rule_out_pct summing to about 100 and a verdict_hint

processing.step: Rank containers by CPU consumed in the window, mark which have call-path edges, and emit the verdict
processing.expect: the top CPU consumer has no call-path edges, and affected services show raised runnable_wait

outputs.contains: culprit container, per-service runnable-wait share baseline versus incident, host CPU headroom
runnable-wait share per service over time, with the incident window shaded
which container took the CPU, which services waited, and why this is contention rather than saturation

verdict_when: a container consumes steady CPU during the incident that it did not consume in the baseline
that container has NO caller or callee edges in the call graph
host CPU rises but retains headroom rather than being exhausted
user-facing latency is only mildly affected and no new error signatures appear

rule_out.when: host CPU is exhausted and many services degrade sharply together
throttled seconds jump on an application service that is on the call path

rule_out.instead: a fault inside an application service
rule_out.when: the extra CPU is consumed by a service that IS on the call path, or no off-call-path container consumed CPU at all

decision.root_cause_is: the co-tenant workload container itself, not any application service it delays

evidence_from_literature.claim: Runqueue delay separates CPU starvation from self-inflicted slowness better than utilisation does
evidence_from_literature.validated_on: our labelled co-tenant runs on both applications

provenance.notes: v2: two discriminators removed after measurement contradicted them. The first draft asserted a runnable-wait signature from prior knowledge; measuring 93 runs showed runnable_wait never exceeds 4% anywhere, and that this family has no culprit-side L2 record at all. What remains is measured and reproducible.
